meta.title: RouteLink — Your OpenWrt router, in your pocket
meta.description: RouteLink is an iOS and Android app for OpenWrt routers: auto-discovery, traffic per device, safe configuration changes, an SSH terminal, an AI assistant and home-screen widgets. Free, open source, no data collection.

hero.title:
Your OpenWrt,
in your pocket
hero.lead: RouteLink is a phone app for OpenWrt routers. Liquid Glass design, made for one hand: check the status, manage devices, change settings and see traffic per device.

features.title:
Everything your router needs,
right at hand
features.lead: From a quick status check to firewall rules — most days you won't need to open LuCI.

discover.title: Auto-discovery
discover.body: Scans your phone's network for OpenWrt, side routers included. Or scan a subnet you name, or type an address.

traffic.title: Traffic per device
traffic.body: With the router plugin: live rates for every device, and usage for any period, per day and per month.

safe.title: Safe changes
safe.body: Every change goes through OpenWrt's own apply-and-confirm: if the app can't reach the router afterwards, the router undoes it after 90 seconds.

ssh.title: SSH terminal
ssh.body: The router's command line inside the app. Confirm the host key once; the app stops if it ever changes.

multi.title: Several routers
multi.body: Add as many as you like and switch from the capsule in the top-left corner.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.body: Ask about your router with your own API key. Before it changes anything, it asks you in the chat.
ai.q: Who used the most data today?
ai.a: Living-Room-TV used 10.0 GB — 38% of today's download. Want me to limit it?

widgets.title: Widgets & alerts
widgets.body: Router status, speed and devices online on your home screen; a notification when it goes down, comes back or sees a new device.

glass.title: iOS 26 Liquid Glass
glass.body: Native Liquid Glass on iOS; on Android the app draws the same design — floating glass tab bar, large titles, rounded grouped lists. Try the tabs below.

demo.title: Demo mode
demo.body: No router at hand? Try everything against the simulated OpenWrt router built into the app.

tour.title:
Every corner of your router,
in plain sight

s1.title: Know it's fine at a glance
s1.body: Model, firmware, load, memory, temperature and internet status; a live traffic chart, devices online, and who used the most today.

s2.title: Every device, by name
s2.body: DHCP leases, the neighbour table and Wi-Fi stations in one list, with vendors and signal. Rename, reserve an IP, block, disconnect, wake — and parental control by schedule.

s3.title: Where the data went, device by device
s3.body: The plugin adds up connection tracking per device MAC — accurate even with software offloading. Charts and rankings for any period, WAN usage per day and month, CSV export.

s4.title: Better Wi-Fi
s4.body: Radios, channels and transmit power at hand. A guest network in one step, shared by QR code; a channel scan that picks the least crowded channel; a security check that fixes what it finds.

s5.title: When something breaks, trace it end to end
s5.body: One-tap diagnosis checks the phone's Wi-Fi, the access point uplink, WAN and DNS in turn. Firewall, port forwards, WireGuard, VLANs, DDNS and SQM — all editable on the phone.

s6.title: When you need to go deeper
s6.body: A built-in SSH terminal with Esc, Tab, Ctrl and arrow keys. An AI assistant that looks up status, devices and logs, asks before changing anything, and masks MACs and public IPs by default.

plugin.title:
Keeps counting
while the app is closed
plugin.lead: routelinkd is a small C daemon on the router. It keeps recording traffic per device, Wi-Fi signal, latency and outages, and runs rate limits, quotas and push alerts. Install it from the app in one tap; it has a LuCI page too.
plugin.p1: Counts IPv4 and IPv6 — accurate with software offloading on
plugin.p2: Rate limits and quotas with tc and nftables, without touching your firewall config
plugin.p3: Push to a Webhook, Bark, ServerChan, PushPlus, Telegram, WeCom, DingTalk or Feishu
plugin.p4: Data stays on your router, and survives firmware upgrades
plugin.luci: LuCI: Services → RouteLink (drawn in the page with demo data; try the tabs)
plugin.appHint: Needs the root account, and the router must reach the official OpenWrt package feeds. If GitHub is slow where you are, enter a download mirror on the same page.
plugin.opkgComment: # OpenWrt 23.05 / 24.10: replace 24.10 and x86_64 with your release and architecture
plugin.apkComment: # OpenWrt 25.12: replace x86_64 with your architecture
plugin.support: OpenWrt 23.05, 24.10 and 25.12; x86_64, aarch64, arm, mipsel and mips.

privacy.title:
Your router
stays yours
privacy.lead: The app talks only to the routers you add — there are no servers of our own. This website uses no cookies and no third-party analytics either.

keychain.title: Passwords in the keychain
keychain.body: Router passwords live only in the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore and are never logged — or not saved at all, if you prefer.

tls.title: Certificate pinning
tls.body: Confirm a self-signed certificate's fingerprint on first connection; if it ever changes, the app stops and tells you.

ssh.title: Host keys
ssh.body: Confirm the SSH host key on first connection. The app's private key stays in the phone's keychain.

nodata.title: No data collection
nodata.body: No analytics, no ads. GitHub is contacted only when you check for updates or install the plugin.

ai.title: AI off by default
ai.body: Once you enable it, only what an answer needs is sent; MACs and public IPs are masked by default, passwords and keys never leave.

confirm.title: Asks before acting
confirm.body: Anything that can cut connections comes with a graded warning; the riskiest steps need the router's name typed in.

download.title: Try it now
download.lead: Free, open source (MIT), no ads. No router? Demo mode lets you try every feature.
download.android2: Updates install from inside the app
download.ios1: iOS 17 or later; Liquid Glass needs iOS 26
download.ios2: Not on the App Store — install with AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly or TrollStore
download.router2: Everything required ships with LuCI; forks such as ImmortalWrt mostly work

footer.note: Screenshots come from demo mode and contain no real router data.

ov.legend: Blue: download, orange: upload. Updated every 2 seconds.

lat.title: Latency and outages
lat.note: The router pings every target every 10 seconds; no reply within 2 seconds counts as loss. Three rounds with every target but the next hop down count as an outage. Red bars: loss; red band: outage.
lat.speedDesc: Measured on the router: TCP handshake latency first, then parallel download and upload for 10 seconds each.

lim.desc: Rate limits and data quotas per device. Limits apply on the router's LAN port and work with software offloading on.

acc.desc: Which domains devices looked up (DNS) and where their internet traffic went. Off by default.
acc.name: Name

nt.desc: Sent by the router itself, so it arrives even when the app is closed. Events within a minute go out as one message.
nt.name: Name
